title: I Took the Glassblowing Glory-Hole Hours to the Mentor Who Left My Gather

parts.text: I stepped into bench three at 10:04 a.m. and mentor Cal was already using my numbered punty. The board said: FORTY-MINUTE HEAT. GATHERS LEAVE WITH THE BOOKING. I was thirty-four, studio tech, holding a clipboard that listed our heat. Cal shrugged. "Mentors keep the heat." I photographed the board, the booking, and his gather in my glory hole. Then I asked for the heat log. At 10:12 the hot-shop desk pinged why Cal's gather was in our hole. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The hot-shop desk can see Cal's gather in glory hole three during our heat.

social.video_title: He left my gather in the glory hole — Part 1/2
social.description: Hot shop, a mentor in my hole, a forty-minute clock he posted. I logged the gather. Would you have asked for the heat log?

parts.text: Cal called it annealing until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the glory-hole still. The punty went back to my numbered rack. Cal ran a slot of their own and told the next mentor atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: MENTORS DO NOT KEEP THE HEAT. I keep our heat on a labeled slate. Cal brown-bags his gathers. The hole finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Mentors do not keep the heat — Part 2/2
social.description: Heat log, numbered punty, and a second line on the board. Was annealing ever our hole?
